I am an old woman now, 81 years, and my strength is not what it was. This small plot near my home I plant with what we eat — I mix the crops together as my mother taught me, so if one fails another feeds us. I have no money for the shop fertilizers or the sprays, but I put the droppings from my few chickens and the ash from the cooking fire on the soil. My grandchildren help me with the digging and the weeding, because my back cannot bend for long, and when the rains come heavy I must ask a neighbour's son for a few days of help with the hoe.
